title.narrative: Envelope 3: Contingency Plan for 48 hours Rapid response for Displacement and Return.

description.narrative: ltpgtTakaful Al Sham (TAS) proposes a flexible, multisectoral emergency response project with a duration of 12 months, designed to rapidly address sudden displacements or returns triggered by emergency events. The project will target populations in transit, IDPs, and returnees across Idleb, and Aleppo governorates—areas where TAS maintains offices, a strong operational presence, and ongoing programming. Additional locations may be identified during implementation to address emerging needs.ltbrgtThe primary objective is to enable a timely, life-saving, and needs-based response by allowing TAS to swiftly mobilize resources and deliver tailored interventions as emergencies unfold. To ensure operational flexibility and comprehensive coverage, the project will span multiple sectors including NFI, MPC, Education and Protection. Other sectors, such as FSL, and WASH, may be added based on identified needs and upon activation of the rapid response mechanism.ltbrgtTAS will maintain continuous monitoring of the security context, population movements, and potential emergency triggers such as renewed hostilities, escalating insecurity, deteriorating living conditions, or natural/seasonal disasters. The organization will also leverage its extensive network of community representatives and local CBOs to ensure timely access to information and rapid resource mobilization for prompt response activation.ltbrgtTo enhance preparedness and implementation capacity, TAS will maintain active framework agreements for essential services and goods, including cash delivery, transportation, Stationary, dignity kits, NFIs, and other critical supplies.ltbrgtUpon activation of an emergency trigger, TAS will conduct rapid needs assessments to determine priority areas of intervention. Assessment findings will be shared with OCHA at various coordination levels, including relevant sub-national hubs. Where needed, TAS will submit timely proposal revisions to ensure the response remains contextually appropriate and aligned with evolving needs. Coordination with relevant clusters and humanitarian actors will be prioritized to ensure complementarity and avoid duplication.ltbrgtIn alignment with the principles of localization and community ownership, TAS will ensure the meaningful engagement of CBOs and community representatives throughout all phases of the project—from risk monitoring to implementation and activity-level oversight. TAS’s longstanding relationships with local communities and authorities will be critical for early warning, needs identification, and activation of emergency response efforts.ltbrgtAdditionally, TAS is currently implementing a national-level project covering all of Syria, further strengthening its capacity to detect, coordinate, and respond swiftly and effectively to emerging emergencies.lt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
